_comment: Registry for the Airtable side of the flooring catalogue: base, tables, field ids, the upsert merge key, batch caps, and the Notion-Company -> Airtable-Supplier alias map. Consumed by .claude/commands/process-price-list.md, .claude/commands/catalog-sync.md, .claude/agents/pricelist-processor.md and (from Phase 4) .claude/agents/airtable-actions-agent.md. Source: live base schema, verified via Airtable MCP 2026-09-10. Field IDS are stable across renames; field NAMES are not — prefer the id wherever the API accepts one.
_maintenance: Goes stale silently when a field is added or a select option is introduced for a newly onboarded supplier. Re-verify with list_tables_for_base (names + ids + types) and get_table_schema (select choices) — bert_schema_export.py merges both because neither is sufficient alone. Last full snapshot: analysis/output/bert-airtable-schema-2026-09-01.json (predates the Length field, added 2026-09-03).

master_flooring_catalogue._comment: Source of truth for every Titan flooring product. 63 fields live; the canonical upload CSV is the first 57 in documented order (the excluded are Price History Log, Price List URL, Promo List URL, Internal notes, Attachments, Attachment Summary, Price History Log v2).
master_flooring_catalogue._merge_field_note: RULE 0. Upsert with fieldIdsToMergeOn: ['fldx3byCOht5HbKmH']. The SKU is immutable and the source of truth — it is NEVER included in the write payload, and no automated process may mint, reformat or 'correct' a stored one. A SKU that looks wrong is escalated, never edited.
master_flooring_catalogue._merge_field_create_exception: CREATE vs UPDATE (2026-09-21, the first real create through this path). On an UPDATE the SKU stays out of the payload, exactly as above. On a CREATE it must be IN `fields`: Airtable matches an upsert on the values in `fields`, so withholding it produces a record blank in the merge key itself. That is not minting — it writes the SKU /process-price-list already minted, verbatim.
master_flooring_catalogue._new_record_source: A plan's `new_product` action carries only the 6 DIFF_FIELDS that catalog_reconcile.py diffs, which is a diff and not a record. Writing just those lands a row with no Supplier, no Collection and no box size in the table Bert quotes customers from. The full record is the matching row of that run's <supplier>_airtable_upload_<date>.csv, keyed on SKU — read it there and write all of it. The plan says THAT a record is new; the upload CSV says WHAT it is. Found on LVP-FAWK-0084, 2026-09-21.
master_flooring_catalogue._stale_supplier_casing_trap: An upload CSV built before 2026-09-21 carries title-case Supplier values ('Floors At Work') while the live options are now ALL CAPS ('FLOORS AT WORK'). Resolve every select against the live option list and leave typecast OFF: with typecast on that difference silently creates a duplicate choice, which is how this base acquired its placeholder junk. Without it the write fails loudly, which is the outcome you want.
master_flooring_catalogue._fields_note: Identity, pricing and matching fields only — the ones automation reads or writes by id. The full 62-field list is in the live schema; the canonical 57-column CSV order is in the bert-airtable-schema skill, which stays the single source for column ORDER.
master_flooring_catalogue._identity_note: Written verbatim from the live record on every matched row. On a NEW row: minted SKU, minted handle, and a deliberately BLANK Lightspeed ID — Lightspeed generates that on create. Never invent or placeholder one. A blank Lightspeed ID is a defect on a `matched` row and correct on a `new` row.
master_flooring_catalogue._helper_note: Appended to the upload CSV for the reviewer, deleted before import. MatchStatus answers 'does this row create or update an Airtable record'; LS Match status answers 'did we find this product in Lightspeed'. They are independent — a row can legitimately be MatchStatus: new AND LS Match status: OK (Canadian Standard 2026-09-03: 292 of 336 rows).

price_history_log_v2._SUSPENDED_2026_09_21: DO NOT WRITE HERE, AND DO NOT CHECK AGAINST IT (Albert, 2026-09-21). Paused in full until he is confident in the master lists — no cost-change row, no promo row, no validation read. A history logged against prices that are not yet trusted reads as authoritative and is not, and that is the one thing this table exists to be. The ids below stay accurate for when it resumes; they are not permission. Resume only on Albert's explicit say-so. See the banner on Table 2 of the bert-airtable-schema skill.
price_history_log_v2._comment: Append-only pricing audit trail. The ORIGINAL Price History Log (tbl1Af1yC6n2KvL7C) was never populated and is superseded — do not write to it.

supplier_aliases._comment: Notion `Company` option -> Airtable `Supplier` select choice. BOTH ARE NOW ALL CAPS (Albert, 2026-09-21): Airtable suppliers were capitalised so Notion, Airtable and Lightspeed mirror each other. That makes 20 of these 25 an identity mapping, and that is the point — what is left is only the entries where the NAME genuinely differs, not the case: FAW -> FLOORS AT WORK, BELLA -> BELLA FLOORING PLUS, CIF (FAOILA) -> CIF DISTRIBUTORS, LEE -> LEE FLOORING, OLYMPIA -> OLYMPIA TILE. Still a lookup, never a case transform — `.upper()` on FAW gives FAW and matches nothing.
supplier_aliases._maintenance: A Notion Company option with no entry here is a supplier not yet onboarded to Airtable — that is the NEW SUPPLIER signal, not an error. Add the pair here when the supplier is onboarded. Never invent an Airtable choice: writing an unknown select value creates a duplicate choice silently, which is how a capitalised column drifts back into mixed case. BRAND is NOT capitalised and is not covered here (Albert, 2026-09-21).
supplier_aliases._lightspeed_is_a_third_namespace: RESOLVED 2026-09-21, verified live: 122 LS suppliers, and the three that differed by NAME rather than case are merged — FAW (317 products) into FLOORS AT WORK, BELLA (288) into BELLA FLOORING PLUS, NORTHWAY BUILDING SUPPLY (67) into NORTHWAY. The Airtable `Supplier` option and the LS supplier record are now the same string for every supplier, so the Airtable value (after alias mapping from Notion's `Company`) is what a CREATE writes to `supplier_name`. This map still does NOT reach Lightspeed by itself — the skill writes that column — but the two namespaces no longer disagree. ls-upload-instructions carried the old short forms and had to be corrected the same day; a create carrying `FAW` now fails outright, which is how it was caught. See lightspeed.json api_shape.supplier._record_rulings_2026_09_21.
supplier_aliases._impressive_added_2026_09_23: Albert added the IMPRESSIVE Supplier option on 2026-09-23, after PL-381 had all 282 Airtable writes refused for its absence (2026-09-22; also PL-226 on 2026-09-14). A first read that afternoon did not find it on fldRZJ5JW4G6Yig8x; a second read confirmed it live (30 options, JL TILE added too), and PL-381 then created 250 IMPRESSIVE records.
supplier_aliases._options_deleted_2026_09_24: The JL TILE and IMPRESSIVE Supplier options were deleted on 2026-09-24 (during the FLOOR & DECOR rename), which blanked Supplier on all 395 records that used them (145 JL TILE + 250 IMPRESSIVE). Albert re-added both; Supplier was restored by record id from the repo's own write records. Deleting a select option in Airtable silently empties every cell that held it — rename an option instead of deleting and re-adding it.

_placeholder_choices._comment: Two literal placeholder values exist in the live base and are NOT real values: `Supplier` as a Supplier choice, and `Stock status` as a Stock status choice. Never write either; treat reading one as a data defect worth flagging.

access._comment: How automation reaches this base today.
access.current: Airtable MCP tools only (mcp__Airtable__*). No API token, no AIRTABLE_* env var, no script calls api.airtable.com.
access.planned: AIRTABLE_PAT scoped to this base alone, added when the write side lands (Phase 4), so batched writes can be idempotent and resumable outside a model turn.
